title: MenoBrain: A Longitudinal Investigation of Menopause and Brain Health
text:
The menopause is a universal experience for women, and many women experience memory problems during
this important time of life. We aim to determine how the brain changes with the menopause and clarify how
changes in hormones, cardiovascular health, and menopausal symptoms influence these brain changes. With
this new knowledge, we can better help women to optimize their memory and brain health as they age so that
they are more resilient to Alzheimer’s disease.

title: Cardiokine FGF16 prevents diabetic cardiomyopathy
text:
The objective of this study is to validate the innovative concept that the unique cardiokine FGF16 protects
against diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) by direct targeting cardio-metabolic reprogramming in multiple diabetic
mouse models and dissect the underlying molecular mechanisms. We will first optimize the doses of a new
FGF16 variant rhFGF16delta33 protecting against DCM in two distinct type 2 diabetic mouse models, and then
we will determine the direct effects and mechanisms of FGF16 on fatty acid oxidation and mitochondrial
function in cardiomyocytes. This project will reveal new insight into the underlying mechanisms behind FGF16
protecting against DCM as well as provide fundamental evidence for rhFGF16delta33 variant as a novel
approach for the prevention of DCM in future clinical studies.

title: Illuminating jumbo phage infection mechanisms: from complex prokaryotic cell biology to novel therapeutics
text:
Bacteriophages kill bacteria through fascinating and diverse mechanisms making them timely therapeutic
candidates to combat antibiotic resistant pathogens. Herein, I study a bacteriophage that potently kills
Pseudomonas aeruginosa using bizarre and exceedingly complex mechanisms to protect its genome from
nucleases while executing early gene transcription and translation. This multidisciplinary project will unveil
molecular mechanisms and future applied potential derived from a unique phage-directed, genome-
containing lipid vesicle

title: Revealing New Therapeutic Opportunities for Kidney Glomerular Diseases by Elucidating the Mechanobiological Functions of Novel Cytoskeletal Structures in Podocytes
text:
The goals of this project are to better understand the pathogenesis of proteinuric kidney disease so that
targeted new treatments can be designed. Podocyte shape and adhesion to the glomerular basement
membrane are critical for maintaining the integrity of the glomerular filtration barrier, which prevents the loss of
blood proteins into the urine. The current proposal aims to gain a deeper mechanistic understanding of the
components and dynamics of the podocyte's cytoskeleton so that we can better understand how podocytes
maintain their unique shape and adhesion within the glomerulus.

title: Role of interleukin-6 signaling on T cell potential of aged hematopoietic stem cells and thymic progenitors
text:
Older adults have increased rates of infections and cancers due to declining immune function, which is likely due
to alterations in T cell progenitors and inflammatory signaling pathways in the aged microenvironment. We will
investigate the causes of T cell decline with age using a newly described mutant mouse model and a novel, in
vitro Artificial Thymic Organoid system, which reproducibly produces all stages of T cell development from a
single stem cell. Our proposed studies will provide insights into the aging immune system and inform future
therapies for regenerative medicine and age-related diseases.

title: The Ecology of Barrett's Esophagus
text:
Pre-cancer cells live in a cellular ecology composed of a variety of different kinds of immune cells, support
cells, and pre-cancer cells. The goal of our project is to characterize that ecology in patients with Barrett’s
esophagus (a pre-cancer) that later developed esophageal cancer, and see if it is different from the ecology of
Barrett’s esophagus tissue in patients that never developed esophageal cancer over a long period of
observation. If we are successful, our measures of the Barrett’s esophagus tissue could be used to identify
cases of Barrett’s esophagus where we should intervene, from those patients that we can reassure and send
home without worry of developing cancer.

title: Lymphatic Support of Neurogenesis and Regeneration
text:
Understanding the regenerative response of the nervous system in models that naturally regenerate is integral
to the development of potential therapies for traumatic brain injury and stroke. The proposed studies in the
zebrafish seek to investigate the mechanisms through which meningeal lymphatics contribute to adult
neurogenesis and regeneration of the nervous system by regulating the immune response and composition of
cerebral spinal fluid. Through these studies we will gain novel insights into the mechanisms that underpin the
relationship between the lymphatic system and promoting the regenerative response of the central nervous
system.

title: Senescent T cells and immunotherapy resistance in head and neck cancer
text:
The proposed studies address the important issues of tumor progression and immunotherapy resistance in
head and neck cancer, which is the sixth most common cancer worldwide with poor prognosis and high
mortality rates. The proposed research has relevance to public health, because it seeks to develop novel
strategies to reverse senescence and immune suppression in tumor-specific T cells and enhance anti-tumor
immunity. Thus, the findings are ultimately expected to be applicable to improve the treatments against
human head and neck cancer and other cancers as well.

title: Systems Bioinformatics Core
text: Systems Bioinformatics Core (Core B) SUMMARY H-CARR is designed to interrogate the genomic, transcriptomic and metabolomic drivers of acquired cisplatin resistance in HNSCC. Projects 1, 2 and 3 are designed to synergize with the ultimate dual objective of: 1) identifying reliable biomarkers of cisplatin resistance and 2) developing strategies for preventing its development or acquisition. Project 1 will generate steady state and flux metabolomic data which will be integrated with the genomic and transcriptomic data generated in Project 2. Together, the datasets will then be validated against human data acquired using non-invasive metabolic imaging and genomic and transcriptomic analysis of human HNSCC circulating tumor cells (CTCs). Core B is envisioned as a Systems Bioinformatics Core which will coalesce the datastreams from all 3 Projects into one coherent multi ‘omics understanding of cisplatin response and development of resistance. Core B, led by Dr. Coarfa is tasked with performing the complex data analysis proposed in each individual Project and developing pipelines for data acquisition, analysis and interpretation which can be rapidly deployed within H- CARR and the broader ARTNet scientific community. Core B, in collaboration with Core A (Administrative) will develop a near real time reporting system for both model (PDX, cell line) generation, analytical pipelines and raw and processed data sharing with other investigators. The Core will leverage existing institutional expertise with big data analysis, along with Dr. Coarfa’s established scientific relationships with the other investigators, to develop a state of the art analytical platform that can be deployed to characterize and understanding acquired resistance across multiple solid tumors and systemic agents.

title: Global Deep Learning Initiative to Understand Outcomes in Major Depression
text:
Our proposed global deep learning initiative unites international experts in artificial intelligence (AI), deep
learning, psychiatry, and neuroimaging to discover brain signatures that predict which patients with major
depressive disorder (MDD) will respond best to repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS). This first
globally coordinated AI analysis of MDD brain data will help discover and understand biosignatures of MDD
treatment response, in diverse cohorts worldwide.

title: The Role of Thyroglobulin in Thyroid Hormone Synthesis
text:
Thyroid hormones, known as T4 (thyroxine) and T3 (triiodothyronine), are synthesized in the thyroid gland on
specific sites within the hormone precursor protein thyroglobulin. In this project, I will create mice with loss of
T4 formation while preserving T3 formation in thyroglobulin which will, for the first time, establish the extent to
which T4 is required for normal development, growth, behavior, hearing, body weight and composition, and
thermoregulation. My studies will aid in our understanding of the defects and treatment of hypothyroidism,
which affects 10% of the world’s population and constitutes the most common congenital endocrinopathy in
humans.

title: TAK1 signaling in Rhabdomyosarcoma tumorigenesis and growth
text:
Rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) is a malignant soft tissue sarcoma that has a higher incidence in
young age children. Even though RMS patients are treated with multimodal therapy that includes
surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy, the survival rate for RMS patients with distant
metastasis is only about 20% to 30%. Our project will identify key mechanisms and molecular
targets to prevent tumor progression in RMS patients in future therapies.

title: GATA Factor Function in Trophoblast
text:
Relevance to Public Health:
Defect in trophoblast lineage development results in early pregnancy loss or leads to pregnancies that are
associated with intrauterine growth restriction or preeclampsia, which are leading causes of maternal death
and premature birth. These are major public health concerns. One of the major causes for pathological
pregnancies is defective development and function of trophoblast cell lineage, which assures embryo
implantation and placentation. Therefore, a better understanding of trophoblast cell lineage development and
function is critical to gain insights into important features of pregnancy loss and pregnancy associated
disorders.

title: Development of a natural language processing (NLP) based therapist tool for culturally responsive care
text: Populations experiencing health disparities often receive worse quality mental health care. There are no feasible, scalable tools to date that provide feedback surrounding culturally responsive care. The purpose of the current study is to develop a natural language processing-based feedback tool to improve culturally responsive care among therapists.

title: Developing the Context-Aware Multimodal Ecological Research and Assessment (CAMERA) Platform for Continuous Measurement and Prediction of Anxiety and Memory State
text:
(3 sentences max)
This project builds the CAMERA (Context-Aware Multimodal Ecological Research and
Assessment) platform, which will fuse diverse data signals from a range of unobtrusive sensors
to continuously predict transient internal states and level of cognitive function. This project will
identify new features of human neural activity, physiology, behavior, and environment related to
memory and anxiety (R61), and test whether we can use multimodal data to more accurately
identify and modulate anxiety and memory performance states (R33). CAMERA will also open a
pathway towards the use of multimodal data and machine learning for naturalistic research and
translational studies related to other complex human internal states and behaviors.

title: Understanding and restoring speech production using an intracortical brain-computer interface
text:
People who lose the ability to speak due to neurological conditions including ALS or stroke have an urgent and unmet
need for therapies that would restore their ability to speak. This proposal is developing a new way to help such patients
using an implanted electronic medical device called a ‘brain-computer interface’ which measures the person’s brain
activity with very high precision as they try to talk, and then outputs their intended words. Bypassing the injured parts
of the nervous system this way requires learning to decipher how individual brain cells in the motor cortex and superior
temporal gyrus – two areas of the brain involved in speaking – work together as a network to produce speech.

title: Controlled Delivery of Adjuvanted Multivalent Fusion Peptide Focused HIV Vaccines
text:
Controlled Delivery of Adjuvanted Multivalent Fusion Peptide Focused HIV Vaccines
Project Narrative
Prolonged antigen exposure provided by the slow release of vaccines into the body is a promising way to
enhance the development of broadly neutralizing antibodies and long-lived plasma cells to retain and recall
those responses, which are critical in realizing a successful HIV-1 vaccine. Our integrated program will
bring a new form of controlled release technology to bear on this problem, along with optimized platforms
for multimeric antigen presentation and adjuvant composition. A cooperative team with complimentary
expertise in immunogen design, formulation, and delivery will identify key determinants of vaccine-induced
durable and protective HIV-1 specific immunity at the cellular, molecular and antibody-epitope level in
rodents and non-human primates to maximize the chances of clinical success.

title: UTSW-UNC Center for Cell Signaling Analysis
text:
The proposed Biomedical Technology Development and Dissemination Center aims to consolidate and distribute
imaging-based technology for the study of cellular signals. The Center will combine computer vision, light-sheet
microscopy, and advanced imaging probes to visualize, control, and model molecular activities at the level of
microns and seconds. The technology will be tested and refined in diverse biological systems and disseminated
to the greater scientific community in partnerships with microscopy core facilities and established distribution
platforms (Addgene, GitHub, ImageJ/Fiji, Applied Scientific Instrumentation).

title: PSP Omics Center of Acute to Chronic Pain Signatures
text:
Identification of molecular signatures predictive of conversion from acute to chronic pain would provide new 
avenues to prevent or attenuate chronic pain conversion, with a wide range of biochemical species that could 
provide a novel multi-molecular signature to chronic pain conversion. The overall objective of this PNNLStanford-Pittsburgh Omics Data Generation Center (PSP-ODGC) is to develop and implement high throughput 
omics-based assays for quantifying a broad and diverse set of molecular players associated with acute to chronic 
pain conversion with the goal to develop predictive signatures as well as inform upon relevant molecular 
mechanisms.

title: Laser particles-based spatiotemporal and dynamic single-cell multiomics
text:
Cells are the dynamic unit of life, interacting with their local and systemic environments and other cells. This
proposal aims to develop a method combining optical and DNA barcodes, that enables the large-scale
acquisition of dynamic single-cell information including cells’ spatiotemporal, morphological, and physiological
changes, cell-cell interactions, and responses to the environment along with their single-cell omics data.
Completing this proposal will offer new avenues to analyze single cells comprehensively.
